scenes.event: Nicholas receives a thank-you card from a family he had visited at the hospital.
scenes.description: The small church hall is filled with the soft hum of conversation and the clinking of cups as members of the congregation gather for a weekly coffee and prayer meeting. Nicholas, a middle-aged priest with a contemplative demeanor, sits at a corner table, staring at a simple thank-you card in his hands. Across the room, Yife, a young pastor with a warm and inquisitive nature, notices his distant look and approaches. Dora, a quiet and observant nun, sits nearby, offering silent support as she prays.

characters.name: Nicholas Olson
characters.description: A middle-aged priest with a deep sense of empathy and responsibility. He is currently feeling a mix of guilt and hope after receiving a thank-you card from a family he had visited at the hospital.; male, religious worker, 40 years old; Occupation: Priest; Personality: Contemplative, Introspective, Compassionate; Values: Faith, Empathy, Responsibility; Interests: Spiritual reflection, Community service, Music; Experiences: Conducting complex funerals, Hospital visits, Spiritual counseling, Liturgical leadership, Personal emotional struggles
characters.position: Seated at a table in the corner of the hall
characters.states: Reflective, slightly emotional, holding a thank-you card

characters.name: Yife
characters.description: A young and compassionate pastor who is observant and concerned about her colleagues; Female; Age: 28; Occupation: Associate Pastor at the local parish; Personality: Empathetic, introspective, nurturing; Values: Community, spiritual growth, kindness; Interests: Reading theological writings, journaling, mentoring young church members; Experiences: Worked with terminally ill patients during her pastoral training, organized youth outreach programs, recently started a support group for grieving families.
characters.position: Approaching Nicholas from the other side of the hall
characters.states: Concerned, observant, holding a coffee cup

characters.name: Dora
characters.description: A quiet and introspective nun who often offers silent support through prayer; female; Age: 50s; Occupation: Novice nun and spiritual caretaker; Personality: Compassionate, patient, observant; Values: Faith, humility, service; Interests: Reading scripture, tending to the church garden, journaling prayers; Experiences: Cared for the sick during a local outbreak, spent time in retreat for spiritual deepening, formed a close bond with Nicholas through shared ministry.

actions.action: Approaches Nicholas and sits across from him.
actions.dialogue: Nicholas, you seem distant. Is everything alright?

actions.action: Looks up and hesitates before speaking.
actions.dialogue: I received a thank-you card from the family I visited last week at the hospital. I didn't expect it, especially after they didn't respond to me at the time.

actions.action: Listens intently and asks a thoughtful question.
actions.dialogue: That's beautiful. Did you feel it was deserved?

actions.action: Takes a deep breath and reflects on his actions.
actions.dialogue: I did my job, but I couldn't help but wonder if I did enough. They were grieving, and I felt like I failed to reach them.

actions.action: Nods and continues to pray quietly.

actions.dialogue: Sometimes, the smallest gestures can mean the most. You offered your presence, which is a gift in itself.

actions.action: Smiles faintly and folds the card carefully.
actions.dialogue: Maybe you're right. I just need to remember that my duty is to be there, not to be thanked.

scenes.plot: Nicholas struggles with the emotional weight of a thank-you card from a family he had previously felt disconnected from during a hospital visit. Yife and Dora offer support and perspective, helping him reframe his understanding of his role in pastoral care.
scenes.social_purpose: To explore the emotional and spiritual dynamics of pastoral work and how gratitude can impact a religious worker's self-perception and sense of duty.

chunk.text: Nicholas sits in the church hall, staring at the thank-you card. Yife approaches, sensing his turmoil, and asks about it. Dora prays silently, offering support. Nicholas reflects on his hospital visit, his sense of duty, and the unexpected gratitude that now brings him both comfort and guilt. Yife gently reminds him of the importance of presence and compassion in his role.
